prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a hit while turning left in Pasadena, Texas, and has shoulder injury. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1175; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the collision you reported. Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather just get to what happened, but fine. It's on the recording, so I'll give you what you need.

Q: Understood. Can you describe where you were when the collision occurred?

A: I was in Pasadena, Texas, driving my car. I was making a left turn at an intersection with a traffic light. The light had been green for me, or at least I thought it was.

Q: Which direction were you traveling, and what did you do before the turn?

A: I was heading north and wanted to turn west. I slowed down, checked for oncoming traffic, and started into the intersection. There was a car coming from the other direction, and I thought it had room to stop.

Q: What happened next?

A: It didn't stop. It came through and hit the front passenger side of my car. My airbag went off and the impact threw me against the door and then back into the seat.

Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt?

A: Yes, I was.

Q: Did you get out of the vehicle, and did you seek medical attention?

A: I got out with help. The paramedics came, and I went to the emergency room that evening. They said I had a shoulder injury, probably from the seatbelt and the door. I've been going to physical therapy since.

Q: Have you had any prior injuries to that shoulder?

A: No, nothing serious. I had some soreness years ago from lifting, but nothing that needed treatment.

Q: Thank you. Is there anything you'd like to add before we conclude?

A: Just that I'd like this handled quickly. I'm still having trouble lifting things, and I'm worried about missing work.

Q: We'll follow up on that. Thank you for your time today.
